extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in probability theory, statistical mechanics, and PDE (large deviations and stochastic processes)
extracted.subtask_description: Lecture-note style treatment of large deviation principles, thermodynamic limits, Cramer's theorem, and PDE methods (viscosity solutions, Hopf–Lax) for proving asymptotic results and small-noise exit problems for SDEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large deviation principle (LDP) with a rate function I
rubrics_metrics.description: We say that {P_ε}_{0<ε≤1} satisfies the large deviation principle with rate function I provided (i) I : Σ → [0, ∞] is lower semicontinuous, I ≢ +∞, (ii) for each l ∈ R the set {ξ ∈ Σ | 0 ≤ I(ξ) ≤ l} is compact, (iii) for each closed set C ⊆ Σ, lim sup_{ε→0} ε log P_ε(C) ≤ − inf_C I, and (iv) for each open set U ⊆ Σ, lim inf_{ε→0} ε log P_ε(U) ≥ − inf_U I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks clarify that for Borel sets E with suitable regularity one has lim_{ε→0} ε log P_ε(E) = − inf_E I, and that the terminology 'rate function' and connections to entropy originate in Ellis. The LDP can be stated equivalently for sequences n→∞ with 1/n log P_n bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Varadhan's lemma / asymptotic evaluation of integrals (Theorem 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {P_ε} satisfies the LDP with rate function I and g : Σ → R is bounded, continuous, then lim_{ε→0} ε log ∫_Σ e^{g/ε} dP_ε = sup_Σ (g − I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses covering by closed sets with small oscillation of g and the LDP upper/lower bounds. This result provides the rigorous justification of formal Laplace-type asymptotics used in statistical mechanics (linking partition-function asymptotics to a variational principle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Converse Varadhan (sufficient condition for LDP via exponential integrals) (Theorem 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the limit in Varadhan's lemma (lim_{ε→0} ε log ∫ e^{g/ε} dP_ε = sup(g − I)) holds for each bounded, Lipschitz g and I : Σ → [0, ∞] is lower semicontinuous with compact level sets {0≤I≤l}, then {P_ε} satisfies the large deviation principle with rate function I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof constructs special test functions g_m to derive the upper bound for closed sets and inner-approximations by closed sets for open sets; this gives a practical route to verifying an LDP by checking exponential integral asymptotics for a class of test functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermodynamic limit and representation via LDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermodynamic limit: for systems with partition functions Z_N = ∫_{Ω_N} e^{-β H_N} dπ_N, define F_N = −(1/β) log Z_N and f(β) = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) F_N when it exists. Recast via distributions P_ε of energy per particle leading to f(β) = −(1/β) lim_{ε→0} ε log ∫ e^{-β ξ/ε} dP_ε and, under a large-deviation ansatz dP_ε ≈ e^{-I/ε} dQ, expect f(β) = (1/β) inf_ξ (β ξ + I(ξ)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the heuristic and rigorous bridge between statistical mechanics (free energy, entropy) and large deviations; the notes further discuss the Legendre transform relation between entropy and rate function (S = −k I^{**}, and in the convex case S = −k I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cramér's theorem conditions and rate function (i.i.d. sums)
rubrics_metrics.description: For i.i.d. R^m-valued random variables Y_k with Z(p)=E(e^{p·Y}) finite for each p∈R^m, let P_n be the law of S_n := (Y_1+...+Y_n)/n. Then {P_n} satisfies an LDP with rate function L(q) = sup_{p∈R^m} (p·q − F(p)), where F(p)=log E(e^{p·Y}) (the Legendre transform of F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: F is smooth, convex, F(0)=0; L≥0 and L(y)=0 at the mean y=E(Y). The theorem explains exponential decay P_n(E) ≈ e^{-n inf_E L} and is demonstrated here via a PDE (Hamilton–Jacobi) approach rather than standard Chernoff/tilting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDE (viscosity solution) method for asymptotics (Hamilton–Jacobi link)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove exponential integral limits like in Cramér's theorem, associate the limit with the unique viscosity solution u of the Hamilton–Jacobi PDE u_t − F(Du) = 0 with initial data u(·,0)=g; then use Hopf–Lax representation (Legendre transform) to identify the limit as sup(g − L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete steps: define discrete logarithmic transforms un from moment-generating objects, prove equicontinuity, pass to a limit u, verify u is the viscosity solution, then apply Hopf–Lax to obtain the variational formula. Assumptions include bounded Lipschitz initial g and finite exponential moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness conditions for SDE solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the SDE dX(t)=b(X(t))dt + B(X(t)) dW(t), if b: R^n→R^n and B: R^n→M_{n×m} are Lipschitz, X_0 independent of the Wiener process and E(|X_0|^2)<∞, then there exists a unique progressively measurable solution with continuous sample paths and finite second-moment bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness is in the usual strong sense (paths equal with probability one on finite time intervals). These hypotheses are the standard setup for stochastic representations of elliptic/parabolic PDE via Itô formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itô's formula and stochastic representation of elliptic boundary-value problems
rubrics_metrics.description: If u∈C^2 and X(t) solves the SDE, then du(X(t)) = Du(X(t))·dX(t) + (1/2) A(X(t)) : D^2u(X(t)) dt where A = B B^T. For the elliptic PDE (1/2)∑_{i,j} a_{ij} u_{x_i x_j} + ∑_i b_i u_{x_i} = 0 in U with u=g on ∂U, the solution admits the stochastic representation u(x) = E(g(X(τ_x))) where τ_x is the exit time from U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the bridge between PDE boundary-value problems and expectation of boundary data along stochastic trajectories; it is used repeatedly in the small-noise exit-probability analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform ellipticity and smoothness for exit-problem asymptotics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume uniform ellipticity: ∑_{i,j} a_{ij}(x) ξ_i ξ_j ≥ θ |ξ|^2 for some θ>0 and that b_i, a_{ij} are smooth. Under these conditions (and connected U) one can analyze exit probabilities and derive precise small-noise asymptotics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform ellipticity ensures coercivity in second-derivative terms and is used in gradient estimates, barrier arguments at the boundary, and passing to first-order Hamilton–Jacobi limits via vanishing viscosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freidlin–Wentzell action functional (rate functional for small-noise SDE paths)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the family X^ε solving dX^ε = b(X^ε) dt + ε B(X^ε) dW, the path-space rate function is I[y(·)] = (1/2) ∫_0^T ∑_{i,j} a_{ij}(y(s))(ȳ_i(s) − b_i(y(s)))(ȳ_j(s) − b_j(y(s))) ds if y(·)∈H^1([0,T];R^n) (and +∞ otherwise), where (a_{ij}) = A^{-1} with A = B B^T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functional quantifies the 'energy' cost of deviations from the deterministic flow and underlies the LDP for sample paths; membership in H^1 (absolutely continuous with square-integrable derivative) is required for finite action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-noise exit probability asymptotics and variational formula (WKB/log-transform result)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let u_ε(x) be the probability that X^ε first exits U through a subset Γ of ∂U. Under hypotheses (U connected, ellipticity, etc.) u_ε(x) = exp(− w(x)/ε^2 + o(1)) uniformly on compacts of U∪Γ, where w(x) = inf_{y(·)∈A} (1/2) ∫_0^τ ∑_{i,j} a_{ij}(y(s))(ȳ_i − b_i)(ȳ_j − b_j) ds and A is the admissible class of curves staying in U until exiting at Γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: set w_ε = −ε^2 log u_ε, derive PDE for w_ε (a vanishing-viscosity elliptic PDE), obtain uniform gradient bounds, extract subsequential limits, and identify the limit as the viscosity solution of a first-order Hamilton–Jacobi PDE whose solution equals the variational formula w.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viscosity solution characterization of the quasipotential w
rubrics_metrics.description: The limit w solves, in the viscosity sense, the first-order PDE (1/2) ∑_{i,j} a_{ij} w_{x_i} w_{x_j} − ∑_i b_i w_{x_i} = 0 in U with boundary condition w=0 on Γ; equivalently w admits the variational representation w(x)=inf_{y(·)∈A} action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of w uses standard viscosity solution arguments: test-function comparisons, ODE perturbations against the flow, and verification of both sub- and super-solution properties. Condition (19) (an 'infinite energy to resist flow' condition) is used to ensure uniqueness and equality of the variational and PDE characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradient and vanishing-viscosity estimates used to pass to the limit
rubrics_metrics.description: For w_ε solving the transformed PDE (−(ε^2/2) a_{ij} w_{x_i x_j} + (1/2) a_{ij} w_{x_i} w_{x_j} − b_i w_{x_i} = 0 with boundary behavior), one obtains local bounds |D w_ε| ≤ C and |w_ε| ≤ C on compacts of U∪Γ (constants independent of small ε) via differential inequalities, cutoff functions, and barrier arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These uniform (in ε) Lipschitz bounds are critical to extract subsequential uniform limits and to justify the passage to the first-order PDE (vanishing-viscosity limit). The notes sketch the differential inequality calculations and maximum-point cutoff argument used to produce the bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of rate functions as entropy and Legendre dual relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Heuristic/statistical-mechanical identification: if P_ε ≈ e^{-I/ε} then free-energy limit f(β) = (1/β) inf_ξ (β ξ + I(ξ)), and using Legendre transforms one expects −S/k = I^{**} and in the convex case S = −k I (identifying rate function with negative entropy up to constants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the thermodynamic interpretation of large-deviation rate functions and ties Varadhan's lemma to classical variational thermodynamic formulas. The text emphasizes this as motivation rather than a formal theorem in that section.
